messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: fncall-proxy error rate spike (7.4% errors over 5m) and structured-output parser queue depth high. sources: /v1/chat/* with tool-call flag; ingest TPS x3 baseline. Auto-mitigation not triggered (thresholds not met for full cutoff). Paging kevin, jamal oncall.
kevin: on it. seeing p95 token latency jump too. are customers reporting failed function invocations or malformed structured-json responses?
jamal: I see stacktrace pointing to structured-parser timeouts when downstream toolpool is saturated. fncall-proxy returning 503s to runtime. Likely cascading backpressure.
kevin: agree. plan: gradual soft-throttle on tool/function calls + restrict structured-json streaming output for hosted tier to reduce pressure. we should avoid full disable if customers rely on it.
maria: tagging into oncall. handoff in 5. I can own coordination and comms to support.
sophie: support queue already has ~12 threads referencing "tool call failed" and a couple enterprise customers seeing partial JSON truncation. urging quick mitigation.
kevin: ok. mitigation steps I propose (in order):
1) apply rate-limit on /v1/function/call for free and trial orgs: token bucket set to 20 TPS per org.
2) flip feature flag to limit streaming structured output to "compact" mode (no repeated schema annotations) for hosted-prod.
3) add temporary caching for identical tool-call signatures (short TTL 30s) at proxy layer.
we can do 1 and 2 immediately, 3 takes more work.
jamal: I can flip flags and patch proxy rules. give me the exact API call to update the dynamo-backed flags store?
kevin: use the admin-config endpoint:

```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/flags/update \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"flag":"structured_output_mode","value":"compact","scope":"hosted-prod"}'
```

and for per-org throttling on the proxy use:

```
# update envoy dynamic route with rate limit matcher
curl -X POST https://fncall-proxy.internal/admin/rate_limit \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"matcher":"org.tier in [free,trial] && path startswith \"/v1/function/call\"","limit":20}'
```

jamal: running flag update now. will validate with canary traffic.
jamal: FLAG_UPDATE: structured_output_mode=compact for hosted-prod applied (via admin API). verify logs: admin-service responded 200.
deploy-bot: rollout noted: flag structured_output_mode -> compact (hosted-prod) by jamal at 2026-10-14T12:37:10Z.
jamal: applying rate-limit rule to fncall-proxy now. pushing policy to envoy fleet.
jamal: RATE_LIMIT_APPLY: policy accepted by fleet controller. starting staggered rollout to 25% of edges.
kevin: monitoring p95 and error rate. also enable temporary debug metric for structured-parser queue length.
kevin: preliminary: errors dropped from 7.4% -> 2.1% in rollout edges. p95 latency reduced ~30ms. good sign.
maria: support update: sending canned note to affected customers and tagging enterprise teams that reported issues. message: "We are applying temporary rate limits and a compact structured output mode to reduce transient errors. No data loss expected; we will update as we monitor." approve?
sophie: yes please include workaround: "If you rely on full structured streaming, consider short-living retry around function call or pin to dedicated capacity"
ashley: tagging product/partners — are there any paid customers scheduled to be fully throttled by the free/trial rule? we should whitelist orgs.
kevin: good catch — we used tier label. jamal can add override list.
jamal: adding allowlist of impacted enterprise orgs now via admin API.
jamal: ALLOWLIST_APPLY: orgs [redwood-enterprise-1, acme-ai] added.
kevin: after allowlist, errors on critical customers return to normal on edges. overall system error rate down to 0.9% and structured-parser queue back to normal.
maria: great. can we keep compact mode for 2 hours while we watch? also keep rate limits in place for 30m then reassess.
kevin: yes — schedule automated rollback in 2h for structured flag and in 30m for rate-limits unless we extend. I'll create a short ticket to document.
sophie: sent support update and opened high-priority threads for the few customers who need deeper follow-up.
jamal: will follow up with a post-mortem draft: root cause appears to be flaky toolpool nodes combined with sudden traffic spike from a popular prompt template causing many concurrent function invocations. we overloaded structured-parser optimistic concurrency.
kevin: notes for postmortem: improve autoscaling for toolpool; add backpressure signals to runtime so it rejects earlier; add circuit-breaker per org to prevent one tenant from tripping global parser; consider defaulting hosted to compact structured output when concurrency > X.
maria: handoff: I'm taking ongoing monitoring and customer comms for the next 45m. jamal, please join SRE review at 15:00 to plan durable mitigations.
jamal: ack. I'll collect logs and SLO impact metrics.
kevin: good job team. final status: mitigation applied (compact structured mode + staged rate-limits + allowlist). monitoring green for now. will reopen thread if regressions.
maria: closing handoff. follow-up owners: jamal (postmortem + infra), kevin (runtime changes + feature), sophie (customer follow-up).
kevin: quick action items (copy to ticketing): [1] postmortem draft (jamal) [2] runtime backpressure changes (kevin) [3] improve toolpool autoscale + health checks (infra) [4] add permanent org circuit-breaker (eng-runtime) [5] update runbook with structured-output fallback pattern (oncall docs).
deploy-bot: NOTE: policy changes applied: structured_output_mode=compact, fncall-proxy rate-limits rolling to 100% after successful canary.
maria: thanks — sending final status to #incidents and #support. good catch everyone.
kevin: we should also add an automated alarm when structured-parser queue > 75% that triggers soft-throttle preemptively. adding to backlog.
jamal: will add a metric and a short alert.
maria: end of thread."
